title: Mini recital: the ending counts
summary: Two pieces for the family again, with a strong ending and a plan for slips said out loud before you play.
materials: the piece from your teacher, with a pencil

figure.alt: A bar of four beats: two played with a rest between them, and the last beat held rather than cut off. This is the strong ending the step asks for: hold the last note, hands off, then bow.

steps.title: The second mini recital
steps.body:
The second recital is the same shape as the first: two pieces, names said, hands in frame, one question from the family. Two things are new.

First, the ending. You learned it first this sprint, so finish strong: hold the last note, hands off, then bow. Do not rush the last bar to get it over with.

Second, the slip plan. Decide now what you do after a slip: keep the beat and carry on from the next bar. Say the plan out loud before you play.

1. Choose the two pieces. One from this sprint, one older.
2. Run each once a day, last line first.
3. On recital day, say the names, play, hold the last note, bow.
4. The family asks one question. Answer it, then write the Practice log.

figure.alt: A bar of four beats ending in a held note, matching the checklist's own line: last note held, hands off, then a bow.

steps.title: Recital checklist
steps.body: Tick each one before recital day.
checklist: Two pieces chosen, one from this sprint and one older
Each piece run once a day, last line first
Slip plan said out loud: keep the beat, carry on from the next bar
Last note held, hands off, then a bow
The family asked one question, and you answered it

steps.title: Record the recital
steps.prompt: Record both pieces in one take, names said out loud, phone where it sees the hands. Slips stay in.
